verdict.root_cause: The evidence does not establish a root cause. Everything the specialists actually measured in ad is clean or uninformative: traces through ad complete without errors at normal latency [tr_cdaa32951ad4], the only error lines in ad's log are OpenTelemetry exporter failures on the background OkHttp thread, caused by DNS resolution of the collector host and not touching the request path [tr_cb5e1e5e4b95][tr_bb7969af7d3e], and both metric attempts failed with HTTP 400 so no error-rate, latency, CPU or heap figure exists for ad at all [tr_f9025118037f][tr_e779ceaa0e52]. The change log shows no proximate trigger, with the last memory-limit toggle reverted ~5.3h before onset [tr_62dee350fb29], and the flagd change query covered only the post-onset window so pre-onset flag flips were never checked [tr_feda815a3c5b]. frontend-proxy and load-generator alerted first and ad alerted a minute later, yet nothing was dispatched against frontend-proxy or frontend. The collector-name resolution failure is the one real anomaly and most likely explains why ad's metrics and traces are sparse or missing rather than why requests failed.
verdict.reasoning: No dispatch produced a mechanism for user-visible failure. Traces are error-free and attribute dominant self-time above ad [tr_cdaa32951ad4]; ad's error lines are telemetry-egress only, in agent frames, with the process still logging at onset [tr_cb5e1e5e4b95]; the sole unresolved host is the collector, not a business dependency [tr_bb7969af7d3e]. Metrics are entirely absent due to malformed queries, not missing series [tr_f9025118037f][tr_e779ceaa0e52], so resource_exhaustion and latency regression are untested rather than excluded. The change log leaves ad at baseline [tr_62dee350fb29] and the flagd window was mis-scoped [tr_feda815a3c5b]. Naming a class here would be asserting more than the board supports.
open_questions: What do ad's error-rate, p95 latency, CPU and heap actually show? Both metric queries were rejected with 400 and must be re-run with a corrected template.
Were there flagd flag changes in the hours *before* 16:14:31? The flagd query window started at onset and ran forward, so pre-onset flips are unexamined.
Why did frontend-proxy and load-generator alert first? No logs, metrics or changes were pulled for frontend-proxy or frontend, and the failure may originate there rather than in ad.
Why does the collector hostname fail DNS resolution intermittently since 2026-10-07T20:28, and does the resulting telemetry gap hide ad-side errors from traces and metrics?

alternatives.root_cause: ad's telemetry pipeline is broken because the collector hostname does not resolve, so ad's failures are real but invisible to traces and metrics.
alternatives.why_not: The resolution failure is confined to one hostname on a background exporter thread and predates onset by a week [tr_bb7969af7d3e]; broad DNS breakage was ruled out and ad's request path shows no impact [tr_cdaa32951ad4].

alternatives.root_cause: A flagd flag flipped shortly before onset drove the ad code path into failure, leaving no artifact or config change in the log.
alternatives.why_not: No flagd child span appears beneath ad in any sampled trace [tr_cdaa32951ad4] and the flagd change query never covered the pre-onset hours [tr_feda815a3c5b], so this is unexcluded rather than supported.

alternatives.root_cause: ad was killed or throttled under a lowered memory limit applied by platform automation.
alternatives.why_not: Every limit reduction has a matching restore and the final revert landed ~5.3h before onset [tr_62dee350fb29]; ad was logging continuously through onset with no restart [tr_cb5e1e5e4b95].

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no change in any metric or log stream should be expected or attributed to this system. The correct next step is investigative, not remedial: re-run the ad metric baseline with a corrected template (the 400 was a client-side rejection, not an empty result) [tr_f9025118037f][tr_e779ceaa0e52], re-run the flagd change query over the hours *before* 16:14:31 [tr_feda815a3c5b], and pull logs/metrics/changes for frontend-proxy and frontend, which alerted a minute before ad [tr_cdaa32951ad4].
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is falsified if a corrected metric query shows a genuine ad-side error-ratio or p95 regression that lines up with onset, or if a pre-onset flagd flip turns up and maps to a revertible configuration, or if frontend-proxy/frontend evidence names a deploy or config change inside the window. Any of those would meet a precondition that is currently unmet and would justify a concrete action. Note also that the one real anomaly - intermittent UnknownHostException on the collector hostname since 2026-10-07T20:28 [tr_bb7969af7d3e] - is a telemetry-egress fault on a background OkHttp thread [tr_cb5e1e5e4b95], so it degrades our ability to observe ad rather than ad's ability to serve; the sparse, clustered trace sampling [tr_cdaa32951ad4] is consistent with that gap, and it means the absence of observed ad errors is weaker evidence than it looks.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is that a real, ongoing fault continues unremediated while the investigation re-runs queries; frontend-proxy and load-generator alerted first and remain uninvestigated, so user-facing impact may be persisting. The risk of the alternative - acting anyway - is higher: the only actions available are rollback_image, revert_config and restart_service on ad, and none of their preconditions are met. The change log records no deploy or config change near onset, with the last memory-limit toggle reverted and paired ~5.3h earlier [tr_62dee350fb29], so rollback_image and revert_config would move ad away from a baseline it is already in. restart_service requires evidence pointing at process state, and there is none: ad was alive and logging sub-second up to 16:13:46 [tr_cb5e1e5e4b95] and its traces completed clean at 0.5-19.7ms [tr_cdaa32951ad4]. A restart would also discard the only live process that is producing the UnknownHostException lines, destroying the one real anomaly we have before anyone has explained it.
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody sees a change, because nothing changes. The services left under an unexplained alert are frontend-proxy, load-generator and ad as seeds, with frontend also affected downstream of ad and flagd still an unexcluded candidate cause for the pre-onset window. Callers of ad - frontend, and through it frontend-proxy and load-generator per the observed call path [tr_cdaa32951ad4] - would have been the ones disturbed by any container recreate, which is a further reason not to recreate one on this evidence.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical multi-service alerting across frontend-proxy, load-generator, and ad with no open incidents to attribute it to. flagd as a one-hop candidate cause hints at a flag/config path, but there is no evidence yet to commit to a class.
